violated_contract: Evidence-binding digests over credential-adjacent identifiers (deployment project numbers, OAuth client ids) must not be built with raw unkeyed SHA-256. Unkeyed digests of low-entropy identifiers are brute-forceable off-line, so a leaked manifest entry discloses the identifier it was meant to hide, and CodeQL (py/weak-sensitive-data-hashing) fails the check-run on every such site. On 2026-09-26 PR #12451's admission evidence binding was rejected by the CodeQL gate for exactly this pattern.
canonical_prevention: Bind evidence with keyed HMAC-SHA256 under a checked-in, non-secret domain-separation label (see backend/utils/external_oauth/admission.py _EVIDENCE_DOMAIN). The key need not be secret for tamper evidence; the keyed construction removes the offline-brute-force and the analyzer finding. Precedent in-repo: backend/utils/referrals.py signs values with hmac.new(..., hashlib.sha256).
